## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two things should be fixed. First, `slugify` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator, so accented titles lose letters and titles written entirely in non-Latin scripts produce an empty slug. Second, the pull-request description does not have the `## Testing` section that `AGENTS.md` requires. Both changed files were read in full, and no critical defect was found.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — A title like `"Café Menu"` becomes `"caf-menu"`, and a title like `"日本語"` becomes `""`. The pattern `[^a-z0-9]+` only allows ASCII letters and digits, so `é` and CJK characters are replaced with hyphens and then trimmed off by `strip("-")` on line 8. The description promises to replace "runs of non-alphanumeric characters", but Python counts these characters as alphanumeric (`"é".isalnum()` is `True`). The tests in `tests/test_slug.py:11-16` only use ASCII input, so this path is never exercised. One fix: transliterate first (`unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)`, then drop combining marks), or match `[\W_]+` with Unicode semantics. Then add test cases for an accented title and for a title with no Latin letters. — Page URLs for non-English titles come out garbled. All titles written entirely in non-Latin scripts get the same empty slug, which can cause URL collisions or empty paths.
- PR body — correctness — The description has no `## Testing` section, which `AGENTS.md:4` requires: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." The body only describes what `slugify` does. Add a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified, for example which test command was run. — Maintainers can't tell from the description how the change was verified, and the project's contribution rule is not met.

(none)

## Strengths
- The new module and test file both start with docstrings that say what they are for, as `AGENTS.md:3` requires.
- The parametrized tests cover trimming of leading and trailing hyphens, collapsing of repeated separators, and the punctuation-only and empty-string edge cases.
